Container.Name: Hyperfocal
Container.Overview: Fast, self-hosted RAW photo culling and library manager. Browse your Year/Event folders, switch between the embedded JPEG and a true RAW render, check clipping with FastRawViewer-style view tools, then rate, label, pick and reject. Ratings, labels, keywords, captions and locations go to standard XMP sidecars that Excire Foto, Lightroom and Bridge read, and edits made there show up here. Rejects are moved (never copied, never deleted) into a _Rejected sub-folder. Culling help shows each burst as a stack topped by its best frame and flags blurry frames, closed eyes and clipping. Zoom in for the full-resolution RAW view, compare 2-4 photos side by side, browse a timeline, keep albums and send them to Immich, find duplicates, manage keywords, geotag from a GPS track, search by what is in a photo and name the people and pets in it (with the optional Hyperfocal-ML companion container), and let the archive integrity monitor warn you (in the app, or through ntfy or Gotify) when an original changes or disappears. Hyperfocal never modifies or deletes your original image files.

Config.Name: WebUI port
Config.Description: Port for the web UI. Put Nginx Proxy Manager (or another reverse proxy) in front of it; see the README for the recommended settings.

Config.Name: Photo library
Config.Description: Your photo library (the folder that holds the Year folders). Read/Write is needed to write XMP sidecars and to move rejects into _Rejected. Set the access mode to Read Only to use Hyperfocal as a pure viewer; it detects that and disables every write.

Config.Name: AppData
Config.Description: Index database, thumbnail and preview cache, sidecar backups and the change journal. Keep it on a pool (cache SSD); /mnt/cache/appdata/hyperfocal is best if appdata is not an exclusive share.

Config.Name: Password
Config.Description: Optional password for the web UI. Leave empty when only your LAN (or an authenticating proxy) can reach it.

Config.Name: Read-only mode
Config.Description: true = view and browse only: no sidecar writes and no moves, whatever the folder permissions.

Config.Name: Rename darktable/digiKam sidecars
Config.Description: Rename IMG_1234.CR3.xmp sidecars (darktable, digiKam) to IMG_1234.xmp so Excire and Lightroom read them. Only when no other photo shares the name; undoable from the history. Turn off if you still edit in darktable.

Config.Name: Reject folder name
Config.Description: Sub-folder that rejected photos are moved into, next to where they were. Folders called _rejected (any case) are always treated as reject folders.

Config.Name: Rescan interval (minutes)
Config.Description: How often to look for new photos and for metadata changed by other apps (e.g. Excire's Save Metadata). Opening a folder in the UI always rechecks that folder. 0 = only at start-up.

Config.Name: Pre-generate thumbnails
Config.Description: Build grid thumbnails in the background after indexing (about 30-60 KB per photo in AppData).

Config.Name: Pre-render previews of recent imports
Config.Description: At idle, make screen-size previews of photos imported in the last days (see below) ahead of time, within the preview disk budget, so the first look is instant.

Config.Name: Recent imports (days)
Config.Description: How far back pre-rendered previews go.

Config.Name: RAW memory cache (MB)
Config.Description: RAM for developed RAW data, so view-tool switches (linear, shadows, highlights, clipping) are instant.

Config.Name: Preview disk cache (MB)
Config.Description: Disk budget in AppData for screen-size previews. The oldest are evicted first.

Config.Name: Index threads
Config.Description: Parallel metadata readers while indexing. Empty = automatic (CPU cores, 2 to 8).

Config.Name: RAW decode concurrency
Config.Description: RAW files developed at the same time (each one already uses every core). Empty = automatic.

Config.Name: People and pets: ML service URL
Config.Description: Optional. The Hyperfocal-ML companion container (face, dog and cat recognition), e.g. http://192.168.1.10:8090. Empty = People and pets is off (names other apps wrote in face regions are still read).

Config.Name: People and pets: ML token
Config.Description: The Token set on Hyperfocal-ML, if any.

Config.Name: People and pets: write names to sidecars
Config.Description: Write the names you confirm to the XMP sidecars: People|Name and Pets|Name keywords, MWG face and pet regions (Lightroom, digiKam) and IPTC person shown. false = names stay in Hyperfocal's index.

Config.Name: People and pets: analysis size (px)
Config.Description: Long side of the image sent for analysis (faces are found down to about 0.6% of it). Larger costs more time to prepare and send, for little gain.

Config.Name: People and pets: photos in flight
Config.Description: Photos prepared and sent to the ML service at once (preparing the next one while the last is analysed). 2 suits a CPU; 3-4 a GPU.

Config.Name: Send to Immich: server URL
Config.Description: Optional. Your Immich server as Hyperfocal reaches it, e.g. http://192.168.1.10:2283. With an API key below, selected photos and albums can be sent to Immich (into an Immich album if you like).

Config.Name: Send to Immich: API key
Config.Description: An Immich API key (Account settings, API keys) with the permissions asset.read, asset.upload, album.read, album.create and albumAsset.create.

Config.Name: Send to Immich: library path in Immich
Config.Description: Optional. If Immich reads this same photo folder as an external library, the path Immich sees it at (e.g. /mnt/media/photos). Photos Immich already has are then found by path and used as they are, instead of being uploaded.

Config.Name: Send to Immich: public URL
Config.Description: Optional. Immich's address for links in your browser, when the server URL above is an internal one.

Config.Name: Archive integrity monitor
Config.Description: Hash every original when it is indexed and verify it again over time; report originals that changed, went missing or became unreadable. Report-only.

Config.Name: Culling: measure photos
Config.Description: Measure every photo once in the background, photos on screen first: sharpness of the subject from the RAW, clipping, and closed eyes with the ML service. Used for series stacks, possible rejects and the best frame of a series. Nothing is ever rejected automatically.

Config.Name: Duplicates: fingerprint photos
Config.Description: Make a perceptual hash of every photo's thumbnail in the background, for the Duplicates report's near-duplicates and series. Exact copies need only the integrity monitor. Report-only: rejecting copies is up to you.

Config.Name: Integrity alerts URL
Config.Description: Optional. Where alerts go: an ntfy topic (https://ntfy.sh/your-topic), a Gotify message URL (https://gotify.example/message) or any webhook (JSON).

Config.Name: Integrity alerts token
Config.Description: Optional. ntfy access token, Gotify app token, or a bearer token for a webhook.

Config.Name: Integrity alerts format
Config.Description: auto decides from the URL.

Config.Name: Verify every (days)
Config.Description: Every original is read and verified once in this many days.

Config.Name: Nightly window start (hour)
Config.Description: Verification runs in a nightly window starting at this local hour (set TZ below).

Config.Name: Nightly window length (minutes)
Config.Description: Length of the nightly window. Outside it, only new and changed files are hashed, at most 4 GB an hour.

Config.Name: Hashing read rate (MB/s)
Config.Description: Read rate while hashing, so array disks are not kept busy (0 = unlimited). Reading also pauses while you are viewing photos.

Config.Name: Time zone
Config.Description: Your time zone (for example America/New_York), for the nightly window.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User ID that files are written as (99 = nobody on Unraid).

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group ID that files are written as (100 = users on Unraid).

Config.Name: UMASK
Config.Description: 000 matches Unraid's share permissions, so sidecars and _Rejected folders stay editable from Excire over SMB.
